title: [GMCP 203.019.04] Adversarial and failure behavior: Human consent, approvals, and interaction UX
goal: Requirement GMCP-203-019-04. Close validation, authorization, isolation, privacy, bounded-resource, cancellation, concurrency, crash, retry, rollback, and recovery behavior. Add deterministic negative, attack, race, corruption, and fault-injection fixtures derived from the vector threat model. Vector outcome: Every consequential MCP action has a consistent inspect-before-run experience showing server identity, exact tool and arguments, data leaving the machine, credentials and side effects, with session and durable consent scoped separately. Approval is revocable, non-transferable and inaccessible to untrusted content; headless denial, accessibility, batching, timeout and emergency-stop behavior are all deterministic and audited. Done means production-path tests and retained evidence prove this work package; task closure or roadmap wording alone is not evidence.
